title: Sequential Decision Making with mHealth Applications

gradingBreakdown.component: Scribing lectures (1-2 lectures per student, typed in LaTeX)

weeklyTopics: Introduction to multi-armed bandits; Robbins (1952) consistency result
Epsilon-greedy and UCB regret analysis (Auer et al. 2002)
Distribution-independent regret bounds and lower bounds
Thompson sampling for Bernoulli rewards (Agrawal and Goyal 2013)
Non-stochastic bandits and the Exp3 algorithm
Introduction to contextual bandits; competing with a policy class
Exp4 algorithm; VE algorithm and regret analysis
Introduction to reinforcement learning / MDPs; UCB for finite-horizon RL (Auer and Ortner 2005)
Guest lecture: real-world mHealth bandit deployment (Elad Yom-Tov)
PAC bounds for multi-armed bandits (Even-Dar et al. 2002), median elimination
Online ranking with top-1 feedback / partial monitoring (Chaudhuri and Tewari 2015)
Guest lectures: contextual decision processes with low Bellman rank (Nan Jiang)
mHealth-specific challenges: costly feature acquisition, non-stationarity, interpretability, on-phone computation, missing data, user engagement
workloadNotes: Advanced graduate seminar co-taught by Susan Murphy and Ambuj Tewari; minimal formal requirements beyond scribing 1-2 lectures each (typed LaTeX notes posted to the course site, 60%) and a final project (survey, paper commentary, or original research, individually or in pairs) split into proposal (5%), poster (10%), and report (25%).
prerequisitesText: Advanced graduate level; comfort with probability and algorithms expected.
textbooks: Bubeck and Cesa-Bianchi, Regret Analysis of Stochastic and Nonstochastic Multi-armed Bandit Problems
Sutton and Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
